method: Actual final GLB rendered in Blender; extracted side/isometric frame sequences and close-ups inspected. Actual CPU Three.js controller pose matrices also rendered with skin/rigid-weapon position cross-checks. No video-URL-only inference, browser screenshot or physical Safari claim.

observations: Authored deep crouch has visible pelvis/waist motion and alternating planted/swing feet.
Chest stays relatively steady while pelvis rotates beneath it; legacy comparison is upright and visibly more rigid.
Rifle remains controlled in low-ready carry; this is not a dedicated aiming pose.
No gross skin collapse observed in inspected views; deep forward lean remains a style limitation requiring user review.
Both feet retain ground support; subtle torso/pelvis breathing visible in the source-driven sequence.
No visible rifle separation or major pose jump across inspected cycle phases.
Support hand wraps the handguard and right hand remains at the pistol grip.
Ground clearance is measured separately on the final skinned asset.
Wrist-point constraints do not establish perfect fingertip collision or equipment collision.
Idle-to-walk blend and cycle-aligned walk-to-idle stop inspected at start/end and intermediate poses.
No gross root jump, frozen torso or floating weapon observed in the corrected controller-pose review.
transitions.reviewRendererCorrection: Initial offline rigid-weapon mapping incorrectly calibrated from Blender imported first-animation pose rather than the glTF default transform. Corrected to direct coordinate conversion and verified sampled actual weapon/magazine vertices. Final review only uses corrected frames.

assessment: Two new imported/contact-retargeted crouch loops ready for user visual review; Stage A remains partial. No new external prone/crawl, cover or armed crouch actions claimed.
limitations: Source style is a deep stealth crouch; approval for military crouch style pending.
No exhaustive fingertip, equipment or arbitrary-obstacle collision verification.
